turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, ma'am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Estella, show our guest the intricacies of this melancholy place.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Pip, observe the clocks around you. Note their eternal pause.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, ma'am. I will observe the clocks, ma'am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will notice how the world outside these walls moves on, while time here stands still, a fitting tribute to a broken heart.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, ma'am. I will look at the clocks, ma'am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Come, Pip. Let me show you the very chamber where time ceased to tick.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, ma'am. I will follow you, ma'am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Lead the way, Pip. And remember, this place holds more shadows than light.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, ma'am. I will go first, ma'am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will notice the clocks, Pip. They stand still, a testament to a moment forever frozen.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Look upon the wedding gown, Pip. It remains untouched, a silent witness to a vow that was never fulfilled.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, ma'am. I see the clocks, ma'am. They do not move.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: The wedding gown, Pip. Notice how it has not been touched since the day it was laid out. It is a symbol of my vow to leave the past as it is.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, ma'am. I see the wedding gown, ma'am. It looks very old, ma'am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Come closer, Pip. I wish to see your face better. Tell me, what do you see in this room?

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I see the wedding gown, ma'am, and the clocks, ma'am. Everything looks very still, ma'am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Do you sense the stillness, Pip? It is as if time itself has paused in this chamber.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I can feel it, ma'am. The room feels very quiet and still, like nothing has changed.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Look into my eyes, Pip. Tell me, what do you see when you look at me?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there! with an impatient movement of the fingers of her right hand; play, play, play!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: So new to him, so old to me; so strange to him, so familiar to me; so melancholy to both of us! Call Estella.
